sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-HA and anti-HLA (W6/32) flow cytometry staining on 721.221 cells; functional NK cell recognition assays were performed on the same cell system but using W6/32-detected HLA-C, not specifically the HA-tagged readout, so function of the HA-tagged protein itself was NOT MEASURED independently.
sites.rationale: All four lines from PMC5490200 (L1–L4) converge on the identical junction: the HA tag is placed after the 24-residue signal peptide (ending in Ala-24) and before the mature N-terminus Cys-25. Python confirms seq[23]='A' and seq[24]='C', matching the canonical sequence exactly. L4 is the strongest clip because it explicitly describes full-length (exons 1–8) constructs and reports confirmed surface display by dual staining. The junction is ≥280 residues from the TM boundary (TM: 308–332), fully extracellular, and the tag is appended to the mature N-terminus, which is the standard validated position for class I MHC N-terminal tagging. Full-length HLA-C*05 and HLA-C*07 constructs spanning exons 1–8 were cloned into a lentiviral expression plasmid with an HA tag inserted immediately after the signal peptide (residues 1–24) and before the mature HLA-C coding sequence. Constructs were transduced into 721.221 cells and surface expression of both HA and HLA-C (W6/32) was measured by flow cytometry on GFP+ cells.

sources.claim: To establish the validity of the system, HA-tagged C*05 and C*07 constructs including the sequence of exons 1–8 of these alleles were generated ( Fig. 3a ), and 721.221 cells were transduced with the respective C*05 and C*07 lentivirus at equivalent multiplicity of infection (normalized using GFP, expressed in tandem from the lentiviral expression vector).
Template used for N-terminally FLAG-tagged HLA mRNA synthesis contained 5′ T7 promoter followed by the V kappa 1 signal peptide, 1× FLAG peptide (DYKDDDDK), and G4S linker.

literature_notes: All five ledger lines (L1–L5) converge on a single physical junction: insert_after_residue=24, the mature N-terminus of HLA-C after signal peptide cleavage. L1, L2, L3, and L4 are from the same paper (PMC5490200) and describe HA-tagged HLA-C constructs; L4 is the most explicit (full-length exons 1–8, surface staining confirmed) and was chosen as the primary supporting clip for Site 1. L2 describes a hybrid construct (HLA-C exons 1–3 fused to H-2Kb exons 4–8) at the same junction; this is weaker evidence for native HLA-C folding and is subsumed by L4. L5 (PMC9619369) uses a FLAG tag with a heterologous SP at the equivalent junction and is reported as a second site entry because it is an independent paper with a different tag. No internal extracellular loop insertions are supported by any ledger line. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are named in the ledger.
